findings.claim: D-37's `retry` cannot work under rulings already made for the same loop: G-47/G-48 run `retest`/`recheck` only after a committed mend, and G-46 lets `pose` end "done" only on a committed mend. D-37 amends none of these rulings and adds no path that reruns the tests.
findings.failure_scenario: A flaky red makes the juror rule DEFECTIVE, so `ask` fires and the owner picks `retry`. In the next iteration no mender commits, so under G-47/G-48 `retest` and `recheck` are skipped and no test runs. Even if a rerun went green, G-46 bars `pose` from ending "done" without a committed mend (landing-design.md:172). The loop goes back to the juror on the old red, and the option fails at the flaky-red case it was added for.

findings.claim: `accept` ends the repair with the tree still red. It breaks the Homes bans on 'a mend that ends unreviewed' (:371) and 'a red shown at the gate' (:370), and handoff has no honest line for it.
findings.failure_scenario: Each of iterations 1-5: juror rules CODE, mend-code commits, recheck stays red, and `review` is skipped (G-48 gates it on recheck not red). At 5 verdicts `ask` fires and the owner picks `accept`. Handoff (:193-196) has only the case 'repair ran', so it prints "Mended on <head>: no new failure.", which is false. The owner then lands five mend commits no reviewer read, behind a gate line that hides the red.

findings.claim: `retry` writes no reply file, so the stall condition 'verdicts since the latest reply file >= 5' stays true once reached. After a retry chosen at a stall, every later iteration asks the owner again.
findings.failure_scenario: The stall ask fires at 5 verdicts and the owner picks `retry`. `hear` keeps only replies (:104-106), so the latest reply file does not change. On the next juror verdict, 6 verdicts follow that reply, and `ask` fires again on every iteration after that. The loop now stops for the owner on each verdict (CLAUDE.md 1.4) until the owner picks `reply`.

findings.claim: D-37 lists only landing-design.md:178/:373 as edits, but `accept` and `retry` contradict lines the ruling does not edit. Under D-02, a ruling that contradicts REQUIREMENTS lines must edit them in the same commit.
findings.failure_scenario: gauntlet-design.md:16 still says the owner 'answers with guidance or leave'. REQUIREMENTS.md:47 (RUN-11) and the ROADMAP Phase 7 goal (ROADMAP.md:89) still say the mend 'repairs a red through a juror-ruled mend read by a reviewer'. An `accept` hands off `ready` for a red that nothing repaired or reviewed. Phase 7 is then built and checked against requirement and roadmap text that the ruled behaviour breaks, and D-02's same-commit edit is skipped.
